samples.text: The period is being run on a manual basis while the incident stays open. The current workaround is this: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. It was chosen because the defect is understood, not because the system recovered by itself. The confirmed cause is stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register, so the override corrects exactly the entries that caused the failure and leaves the rest of the mapping as it was. That is a narrow and deliberate holding position, and it is provisional. For readers deciding whether to wait, the override is enough to complete this period but not enough to trust the next one. It depends on a hand edit to a table that is still maintained by hand, so the same stale entry, or a new one, can return on the next refresh. Teams can use the valuation produced under the override for the current period. They should not assume that later runs are safe until the incident

The valuation run failed because of a reference data defect, not an infrastructure fault. The confirmed cause is this: stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. That was not the first explanation. At triage, the working hypothesis was recorded as overnight ERP outage, and the early investigation followed that line. The evidence then excluded it, because ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the outage ruled out, the trace moved to the agency codes that feed the inventory valuation service, and the stale entry was found in the mapping. The review classifies the underlying fault as a gap in how the table is governed: control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer.
